stop_condition: R17-F1 is fixed with a pairing leg that observes the shipped artifact running; the BARE-SUBSTITUTION-CENSUS block's membership and every one of its dispositions are independently re-derived and hold; and no claim the change set writes into durable code comments, notes or governing numbers is false against the target interpreter.

findings.evidence:
The census's stated rule reads: `set -e` inherits into subshells (INCLUDING COMMAND-SUBSTITUTION SUBSHELLS), but a subshell aborting on its OWN internal set -e trip does not itself abort the PARENT shell. The parenthetical is false on this file's own interpreter. MEASURED on /bin/bash 3.2.57 (this file's shebang is #!/bin/bash; no `shopt -s inherit_errexit`, no `set -o posix` anywhere in the file; `shopt inherit_errexit` on this build answers `invalid shell option name` -- the option did not exist until bash 4.4, and even where it exists it is OFF by default):
  /bin/bash -c 'set -e; x=$(false; echo AFTER-RAN); echo x=[$x]'   -> x=[AFTER-RAN], rc=0   (errexit UNSET inside $( ))
  /bin/bash -c 'set -e; ( false; echo SUBSHELL-AFTER ); echo P'    -> rc=1                  (errexit IS inherited into ( ))
The bash manual's own wording for inherit_errexit is the confirmation: "command substitution inherits the value of the errexit option, INSTEAD OF UNSETTING IT in the subshell environment."

The rule is covered by a blanket verification claim at :262-270 -- "All of the above was checked against this exact bash build with disposable probe scripts before being relied on" -- while the three results it then names as independently reproducible (`local var=$(false)` reaching rc 0; `echo "$(false)"` reaching rc 0; `${u:-$(false)}` NOT reaching) are exactly the three I DID reproduce. The inheritance claim is the one rule in the block that is not among the named-reproducible results, and it is the one that is false.

THE RULE IS LOAD-BEARING FOR A DISCOVERY THAT DOES NOT EXIST. :3606-3613 states of get_labels(): "a non-zero one aborts the WHOLE PROCESS right there, before `rc=$?` ever executes -- MEASURED directly: calling this function bare (x=$(get_labels "$tid"), no wrapper) against bd show <nonexistent-id> ... aborts before printing anything." A/B on the exact pre-fix form from the diff (`local raw rc` / `raw=$(bd show "$1" --json 2>/dev/null)` / `rc=$?`) against the exact post-fix form (`|| rc=$?`), stub exiting 1:
  A pre-fix,  bare x=$(get_labels_PREFIX bogus)  -> [INTERNAL] rc=$? DID execute, rc=1 ; outer rc=1
  B post-fix, bare x=$(get_labels_POSTFIX bogus) -> [INTERNAL] rc captured, rc=1        ; outer rc=1
  C pre-fix,  if x=$(get_labels_PREFIX bogus)    -> rc=$? DID execute ; if-false ; REACHED ; rc=0
  D post-fix, if x=$(get_labels_POSTFIX bogus)   -> rc captured      ; if-false ; REACHED ; rc=0
`rc=$?` executes on every path, because get_labels is only ever invoked THROUGH a command substitution, where errexit is off. The abort in A is real but is caused by the function's own correct `return 1` reaching the caller's bare assignment -- and B aborts identically. Pre-fix and post-fix are behaviourally indistinguishable in all four scenarios. get_labels() and get_parent_epic() were not defective; the census indexes them at :391-397 under "GENUINE DEFECTS, FIXED THIS ROUND".

The forward-looking warning at :3633-3634 and :421-423 -- "The next caller that writes the obvious form -- a plain, unwrapped x=$(has_label ...) or x=$(get_labels ...) -- reopens exactly this" -- is false in the same direction: scenario B is that caller, and it behaves the same after the fix as before it.

SECOND-ORDER: the rule conflates two constructs that behave OPPOSITELY here, and this file contains both. `( )` subshell bodies DO inherit errexit; `$( )` bodies do not. qa-gate.sh defines two subshell-body functions (review_dir_is_review_subdir at :7512, design_dir_is_spec_dir at :8764). Both happen to contain no command substitutions, so nothing is unguarded today -- but a reader applying the stated rule cannot tell those two functions apart from the ~19 ordinary helpers the census disposes of, and the rule gives the wrong answer for both classes.

THIRD-ORDER, and the part that actually costs coverage: at :433-441 the census correctly identifies that review-check.sh (no `set -e`) has a DIFFERENT hazard class -- "a failing bare command substitution ... degrades into a variable holding wrong or empty data and execution continuing, never an uncontrolled process exit" -- and declares it out of scope. That is exactly the class that also applies INSIDE every qa-gate.sh function invoked via $( ), which is most of them. The census does not see this, because its rule says those bodies abort. So the sweep's own stated scope silently excludes a real class in the file it swept.

WHAT IS NOT WRONG, verified independently so the correction stays bounded: I re-derived the census membership with a quote/nesting-aware scanner that resolves each substitution's matching close paren and classifies the syntactic context ANYWHERE on the line (not anchored at line start, so it does not share the implementer's blind spot). It finds exactly 317 assignment-form command substitutions -- the census's own number. Zero `local x=$(...)`, zero `export`/`declare`/`readonly`/`typeset x=$(...)`, zero `arr=( $(...) )`, zero `arr[i]=$(...)`, zero multi-assignment `a=1 b=$(...)` anywhere in the file; the only non-line-start aborting-form sites are ten, and every one is either an `if [!] raw=$(...)` condition or a substitution inside a message string. Of the 81 unguarded ones, all fall inside declared categories (22 safe-last-stage, 19 callee-contract, 17+7 prior-validation jq extractions, 16 date). No category is unsound and no member is missing. The defect is the rule and the two non-defects it produced, not the sweep.
findings.description: The BARE-SUBSTITUTION-CENSUS is this round's deliverable and is explicitly normative -- it exists because the R16-F1 fix comment asserted a class was closed without checking the file, and that comment is preserved three screens below as the cautionary tale. Shipping it with a false shell-semantics rule at its head, asserted as empirically verified, reproduces that failure one level up: a confident claim about a class, stated as measured, that does not reproduce. It also writes two non-defects into the durable record (census index, the get_labels/get_parent_epic headers, and the task notes' ADDITIONAL DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED paragraph), and leaves future readers a rule that is wrong in both directions -- over-predicting aborts in $( ) bodies, under-predicting them in ( ) bodies, and hiding the silent-wrong-data class the census itself correctly names for the sibling script. Remedy is bounded and does not touch code: correct the rule at :252-256 to state that command substitution UNSETS errexit on bash 3.2 (with the measurement) while explicit ( ) subshells inherit it; restate the get_labels/get_parent_epic change as a contract-hygiene/idiom change rather than a defect fix, with the A/B showing pre- and post-fix are indistinguishable; drop or correct the 'next caller reopens exactly this' warning; and either fold the silent-wrong-data class into the census's scope statement or name it as a known residual the way review-check.sh's is named. The code changes themselves are behaviour-preserving and can stay. (Also at :3622: 'sec -e' for 'set -e' -- cosmetic, fix while in there.)

findings.evidence: Lines added by THIS change set state the governing headroom figure for the per-spec cap: ':653  unrecorded-review-artifact.test.sh 170/170 in 676.60s real (75.2% of the cap)'; ':660  Per-spec wall-clock cap (seconds). HEADROOM IS 1.31x, NOT 3.7x.'; ':669-670  unrecorded-review-artifact.test.sh, 170/170 assertions, exit 0 -- 676.60s (implementer), 684.91s (QA's independent confirming run), 711s (the implementer's own contended full-tier run)'; ':674  900/684.91 = 1.31x against the worst figure anyone has measured here'. The same change set's own notes report this file now runs 185/185 in 756.16s. 900/756.16 = 1.19x, and 756.16/900 = 84.0%, not 75.2%. Every one of those numbers is stale by exactly this round's growth, and they were added, not inherited. The paragraph they sit in warns about precisely this: 'The 3.7x figure went stale exactly the way it once replaced a stale "~5x": it reasoned from the worst case measured at the time ... and nothing flagged it when a later spec grew past that worst case.' The cap is not decorative -- design-review-record.test.sh is currently FAILING at this same 900s cap (tracked on fcq3), which is named four lines below the stale figure.
findings.description: CONTRIBUTING.md's rule is that a number carries the command that produced it and the commit it was measured at. The header is the one place the project reasons about whether SPEC_TIMEOUT_S is safe, and it now understates the tightest spec by 15 assertions and ~71s while the ratio it publishes (1.31x) is 10% better than reality (1.19x). Remedy: update :653, :669-670 and :674 with the round's measured figures and the command that produced them, and re-state the percentage. Separately -- a ruling, not a finding: 84% SHIPS for this task. The tier passes with the file inside, the growth this round (+71s) is half the prior rate (~147s), and requiring a second split as a precondition of a P0 fix is scope creep. But 144s of headroom is one ordinary round, the last split in this file was done reactively AFTER crossing, and a sibling spec is over the cap right now. File the split as a follow-up task with a concrete trigger (e.g. split at 800s or at the next round that adds assertions here, whichever comes first) rather than leaving it as a header note.
